grh_397a8dab9e3509e02815.title: Playboy
paragraphs: Pat Blair has always been Rivers End's charming, irresponsible playboy, and a damaged heart has kept him out of military service while his old schoolmate Bob Sims fights overseas. Gossip becomes especially ugly when Pat spends time with Bob's wife Lily, leading Bob to write Lily that she need not remain tied to him if she prefers Pat. Then Pat is injured in an automobile accident after trying to avoid blind Elizabeth Elliott as she crosses the street; Elizabeth suffers a broken hip and fears she will never walk again. Dr. Christian sends Pat to cheer her, and the supposedly selfish playboy devotes himself to her recovery. He helps arrange her settlement, sells securities left by his mother to pay part of it himself, tends her garden and becomes the one person who can make her laugh and believe she will walk. Bob returns on furlough just as Lily unexpectedly finds Pat coaching Elizabeth through her first steps. Lily angrily condemns Pat, but Elizabeth defends the friend she has come to know. The emotional confrontation makes Elizabeth forget her fear long enough to walk, while Bob finally hears Lily's explanation and recognizes how badly gossip and assumption distorted what happened. Christian's lesson is that Pat contains real generosity despite his faults, and that judging any of them by reputation alone misses the whole person.

This [[show|dr-christian|Dr. Christian]] broadcast aired on October 24, 1945. It is listed as episode 361 in the archive. [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]] carried the broadcast. The cast includes Jean Hersholt and Rosemary De Camp. Other credited names include Bob Anderson as announcer.
The surviving recording runs about 25 minutes. The broadcast is also associated with [[org|org.b199d95f77b6c241|Vaseline]].

grh_3942c730c0d4c4829fb6.title: Mademoiselle Modiste
paragraphs: Paris hat-shop girl Fifi dreams of a larger life and loves army officer Etienne, whose aristocratic uncle considers her unsuitable. grh_3993cf9ed2d6224e3fae.title: This Is Where I Came In
paragraphs: Returning serviceman Perry Tate is preparing to marry Mary Mason when actress Vivian Hall produces an old letter in Perry's handwriting that reads like a proposal to her. Perry explains that years earlier, while helping Vivian prepare props for a stage play, he copied the romantic letter directly from the script as a joke and signed it. Vivian nevertheless intends to use the document as proof of a promise to marry and as publicity to revive her career. Dr. Christian confronts her with a copy of the play and gets Vivian to reenact the scene in which the heroine burns the letter. Carried away by her own performance, Vivian accidentally sets fire to the real document. Christian puts out the fire, but Perry's signature has burned away, destroying the leverage Vivian meant to use against his real marriage plans.
This [[show|dr-christian|Dr. Christian]] broadcast aired on May 2, 1945. It is listed as episode 336 in the archive.
The surviving recording runs about 26 minutes.

Perry explains that years earlier, while helping Vivian prepare props for a stage play, he copied the romantic letter directly from the script as a joke and signed it. Vivian nevertheless intends to use the document as proof of a promise to marry and as publicity to revive her career. Dr. Christian confronts her with a copy of the play and gets Vivian to reenact the scene in which the heroine burns the letter. Carried away by her own performance, Vivian accidentally sets fire to the real document. Christian puts out the fire, but Perry's signature has burned away, destroying the leverage Vivian meant to use against his real marriage plans.

This Dr. Christian broadcast aired on May 2, 1945. It is listed as episode 336 in the archive.

The surviving recording runs about 26 minutes.

grh_39ab8bff94b96054728f.title: The Return -1
paragraphs: World-weary traveler Reeser reaches Bizerte searching for a place where there is no struggle. A blind beggar leads him through a mysterious wall into a seemingly perfect world where every need is met, love is effortless and nothing resists him. Reeser gradually realizes that perfection has eliminated challenge, individuality, effort and meaningful choice, so he rejects it and returns to the ordinary world. Back in Bizerte he discovers that what seemed like a brief experience in the perfect place has cost him a full year.
This [[show|escape|Escape]] broadcast aired on November 9, 1952. It is listed as episode 156 in the archive.
CBS high-adventure anthology mixing original radio stories and literary adaptations.
